To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
any digital modulation can be synthesized as the superposition of a small number of time limited pulses, and that the spectral characteristics of these modulations can be derived in closed form.

any digital phase modulations can be expressed as a finite superposition of amplitude modulated pulses, that the AMP decomposition of a signal can be obtained from a single optimized pulse, and that the autocorrelation and the spectrum of half-integer index phase modulations can both be computed very easily.
any digital phase modulation can be expressed as a superposition of time limited amplitude-modulated pulses, and this decomposition can be computed exactly.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of digital modulations by superposition of AM pulses.
the exact and approximate AMP synthesis and the spectral properties of binary phase modulations.
the construction of digital phase modulations by the superposition of time limited pulses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
any constant amplitude digital modulation with binary phases can be built as the superposition of a finite number (usually 2) of AM pulses.
any binary phase modulation is a sum of time limited AM pulses and that a single pulse can be used for a good approximation.
the AMP synthesis is a very powerful and efficient method for the construction of digital phase modulations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
any constant amplitude digital phase modulation can be built as an AMP decomposition, which is an exact decomposition for half-integer indices and a very good approximation for integer indices.
any constant-amplitude phase modulation can be synthesized with good accuracy by a superposition of a few time-limited pulses.

any constant amplitude phase modulation can be expressed as a set of shifted AM pulses, with a simple formula for the autocorrelation and a very simple expression for the power spectrum, and that this signal can be synthesized with good accuracy by a simple pulse shape.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the AMP decomposition of a signal is an alternative to the Fourier series decomposition, which has a number of advantages: (i) it is more general (ii) it is simpler and faster to calculate (iii) it is easier to optimize (iv) it is easier (and sometimes possible) to build a good approximation of the original signal by superposing only a few pulses.
any binary modulation can be expressed as a linear combination of AM pulses, and this decomposition can be used for the design of digital modulations.
any digital modulation can be expressed as a superposition of time limited pulses, which is very interesting for applications in digital communications.
